message.reasoning:
We need to mark against rubric. Let's analyze the submission.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight, max 40, levels 7-10 accomplished, 4-6 adequate, 0-3 deficient). The submission describes coral reef monitoring mission, GBR, users (marine/conservation scientists), why needed (bleaching, acidification, resolution). References included (4 URLs). Some technical issues: "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" - actually pH dropped 0.1, ~30% increase in H+ concentration, so phrasing "30 percent more acidic" is commonly used but technically imprecise; acceptable. "In 2016, a bleaching killed 60 percent of the reef's coral. In 2017, another 50 percent perished." This is inaccurate/exaggerated - 2016 bleaching killed ~22% of corals in GBR (or 29% loss of shallow-water corals), 2017 another ~20%. Saying 60% and 50% is wrong. Also "geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km" is a major technical error - GEO is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO. That's in project plan section, but relevant to mission concept/design logic. Also "keeps the satellite fixed above the reef at all times" - GEO at 600 km impossible. This is a significant technical error. However C1 is about mission concept and rationale, not detailed orbit. Still, the mission concept includes orbit choice. The concept is clear, users identified, rationale strong, references. But technical inaccuracies reduce. I'd say Adequate to Accomplished boundary. The description is clear and complete, relates function to users, references. But the orbit error and exaggerated statistics undermine. I'd place at Adequate high (6) or Accomplished low (7). Given the rubric: Accomplished requires "clear and complete description of mission goals, objectives, and requirements. Clearly relates required mission function to users and their needs. References to literature as appropriate." The submission does this well. The technical error is in the plan section, not the concept. But the concept mentions "near-real-time relay" and "dedicated satellite monitoring" - goals are somewhat vague (no specific requirements like resolution, revisit, spectral bands). Objectives not quantified. So "lack of specific details" fits Adequate. I'd give 6/10 → 24/40.

C2: Project plan (30% weight, max 30). Gantt chart included, task descriptions, deadlines, completed stages. Plan is detailed, covers background research, launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL, STK design/simulations, editing. However, no explicit provision for contingencies/variations. The rubric Accomplished requires "robust and has provision for project variations and contingencies. The plan fits within the narrative set out by the mission concept – the student makes clear why the plan is developed this way in the context of the mission. Appropriate references to information sources are included." The plan does fit the mission narrative (coral monitoring → launch/orbit/comms). But no contingency. Information sources: references in C1, but the plan section doesn't list planned information sources explicitly beyond "research existing satellites" and "syllabus work". The task requires "List the information sources you plan to use." The submission has 4 references in the concept section, but not a dedicated list of planned sources for the project. That's a partial miss on R5. The Gantt is clear. I'd say Adequate to Accomplished. Given no contingency and no explicit information sources list, Adequate high: 6/10 → 18/30. Or Accomplished low 7 → 21/30. The plan is quite detailed and feasible. But the rubric's Accomplished explicitly requires contingencies and references to information sources. Missing both. So Adequate: 6 → 18/30.

C3: Preliminary progress (10% weight, max 10). Evidence: completed STK tutorials 1-4, read Asner brief, researched bleaching, Gantt shows completed background research, project planning, mission concept, strategies. But no actual technical results (no orbit calculations, no link budget, no STK simulation outputs). The rubric Accomplished: "Good preliminary set of results included with brief description and/or interpretation. Clearly on track for completion." Adequate: "Minor work completed on the project. Results description or interpretation may be insufficient." The submission has minor work: tutorials completed, research done, but no results. The orbit choice is stated but wrong. I'd say Adequate: 5/10 → 5/10. Maybe 4. Let's give 5.

C4: Report presentation (20% weight, max 20). Structure: headings, clear writing, references with superscript numbers and URL list. Gantt chart labelled with legend in text. However, references are just URLs, not proper citations (no author, title, date). The rubric says "References in text match reference list (and vice versa) and are cited properly." They match (1-4), but not properly formatted. Also the Gantt chart image is clear. Writing is good, some informal phrasing ("stitching together", "maybe only one is required"). Formatting consistent. I'd say Adequate to Accomplished. The report is easy to read, well-structured. References are weak (URLs only). I'd give 7/10 → 14/20. Or 6 → 12/20. The rubric Accomplished requires "References in text match reference list (and vice versa) and are cited properly." They are not properly cited (no author/title). So Adequate: 6/10 → 12/20. But presentation is quite good otherwise. I'll give 6.

Now requirements:
R1: Design simple space-mission concept benefiting Australia; explain purpose, users, rationale. Met: yes. Where: Mission Concept & Rationale.
R2: Relate preliminary plan to mission's space segment, applying course material such as launch and orbits. Partial: plan includes launch specifics, orbit specifics, but orbit error (GEO at 600 km) shows misapplication. Also "calculate COEs & AOEs" mentioned. So partial. Where: Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, Orbit Specifics.
R3: Select software package. STK is mentioned (STK Design, STK Simulations, STK tutorials). Met: yes. Where: Project Plan & Preliminary Progress.
R4: Project plan with Gantt chart or timetable. Met: yes. Where: Image 1.
R5: List information sources planned. Partial: references in concept section, but not a planned source list. Where: Mission Concept & Rationale footnotes.
R6: Preliminary technical content demonstrating sufficient work. Partial: tutorials completed, research, but no technical results. Where: Project Plan & Preliminary Progress.

Technical issues:
- "geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km" — GEO altitude is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO. Major error.
- "In 2016, a bleaching killed 60 percent of the reef's coral. In 2017, another 50 percent perished." — inaccurate; actual mortality lower (~20-30% each year). Exaggerated.
- "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — technically pH decreased by 0.1, representing ~30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration; commonly stated but imprecise.
- "current satellites have only mapped Great Barrier Reef depths to a resolution of 100 meters per pixel" — plausible but needs source; reference 3 is deepreef.
- No specific mission requirements (resolution, revisit time, spectral bands, data rate) — concept lacks quantitative requirements.
- Gantt chart: "Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue." But background research shows gold in weeks 2-3 and blue in weeks 4-8, which is odd (ongoing). Also "Deadlines are indicated by red lines" — only one red line at week 4? Actually red line at start of week 4 and maybe end? The image shows red vertical lines at week 4 boundary and week 10? Hard to tell. Minor.
- "Weeks 7 and 8 are reserved for review" but Gantt shows editing in weeks 9-10. Inconsistency.
- "Final report is due on 20/11/20 at 5pm" but Gantt ends week 10 (16/11). Minor.

Overall: The report is a solid preliminary submission with clear mission concept and detailed plan, but has significant technical errors (orbit altitude) and lacks quantitative requirements and contingency planning. Mark: C1 24/40, C2 18/30, C3 5/10, C4 12/20 = 59/100. That seems reasonable. Maybe C1 24, C2 18, C3 5, C4 12 = 59. Or C1 28 (7/10), C2 21 (7/10), C3 5, C4 14 (7/10) = 68. Let's think more carefully.

C1: The mission concept is actually quite strong: clear problem, users, rationale, references. The lack of specific requirements is a detail issue. The orbit error is in the plan, not the concept. I'd lean Accomplished low: 7/10 → 28/40. But the rubric says "clear and complete description of mission goals, objectives, and requirements." There are no explicit requirements (e.g., spatial resolution, revisit frequency, data latency). The goals are qualitative. So "lack of specific details" → Adequate. 6/10 → 24/40. I'll stick with 24.

C2: Plan is detailed, Gantt, task descriptions. Missing contingency and explicit information sources. Adequate: 6/10 → 18/30. Could be 7 if we consider the plan robust enough. But no contingency is a clear miss for Accomplished. 6.

C3: Minor work: tutorials, research, no results. Adequate: 5/10 → 5/10. Could be 4. 5 is fine.

C4: Good structure, clear writing, but references are just URLs, not proper citations. Also some informal language. Adequate: 6/10 → 12/20. Could be 7. The report is easy to read and well-formatted. The rubric's Adequate says "not at a professional level but does make use of headings... writing is just ok... references mostly cited correctly." The references are not properly cited (no author/title). So 6.

Total: 24+18+5+12 = 59.

Let's ensure JSON format. Need criteria array with id, level, mark, evidence, reasoning. Requirements array. Technical issues array. Overall.

Evidence quotes must be exact contiguous text <=25 words. For C1: "Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring." That's 14 words. Or "A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events." 24 words. Good.

C2: "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page." 20 words. Or "Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines." 14 words.

C3: "I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4." 28 words? Let's count: I(1) have(2) read(3) the(4) brief(5) of(6) Asner’s(7) monitoring(8) system(9) in(10) Hawaii(11), researched(12) into(13) how(14) coral(15) bleaching(16) occurs(17) and(18) its(19) severity(20), and(21) also(22) completed(23) STK(24) tutorials(25) 1(26), 2(27), 3(28) &(29) 4(30). 30 words. Too long. Use shorter: "completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4." 7 words. Or "My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km" 13 words. That's technical progress? It's a stated choice. Use that.

C4: "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart." 10 words. Or "Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page." 9 words. For presentation, maybe quote the reference list: "¹ https://www.noaa.gov/education/resource-collections/ocean-coasts/ocean-acidification" but that's a URL. Better: "Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet" 13 words. Shows writing. Or "This stage is complete as part of the preliminary report." 9 words.

R3 yes, where "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress — STK Design & Simulations". R4 yes, where "Image 1". R5 partial, where "Mission Concept & Rationale footnotes". R6 partial, where "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress".

Technical issues: list with where and issue.

Overall: <=60 words. "A clear, well-structured preliminary report with a strong mission rationale and detailed Gantt plan. However, it contains a major orbit error (GEO at 600 km), exaggerated bleaching statistics, lacks quantitative mission requirements, contingency planning, and a proper reference list. Preliminary technical results are minimal." That's 45 words.
